sections.content: You know the present perfect from A2 Unit 1, with *ya* and *todavía no* from A2 Unit 2. It connects a past development with the present, so it is useful for changes that matter now, especially with *últimamente* and *en los últimos años*. This lesson adds *acercarse* and *distanciarse*.

items.spanish: Hemos cambiado mucho desde que terminamos la universidad.
items.english: We have changed a lot since we finished university.

items.spanish: Últimamente nos hemos acercado porque tenemos más tiempo para hablar.
items.english: Lately we have become closer because we have more time to talk.

items.spanish: Nos hemos distanciado un poco, aunque seguimos confiando el uno en el otro.
items.english: We have grown somewhat distant, although we still trust each other.

items.spanish: Nuestra relación ha mejorado porque hemos aprendido a escucharnos.
items.english: Our relationship has improved because we have learned to listen to each other.

sections.content: Use the present perfect when the change is relevant to the present situation. The time expression and the speaker's perspective help determine whether this tense is natural.
